core_obligations: Take a short exact sequence of modules and write down the associated long exact sequence of Ext groups (proof lines 13668-13681).
Read off that vanishing of Ext in degree one makes the Hom sequence exact, i.e. gives injectivity (proof lines 13682-13684).
Conversely, use the identification of Ext with derived functors and their vanishing for injective modules (proof lines 13685-13689).
proof_roadmap: Display the long exact sequence (proof lines 13668-13681).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises injective modules by the vanishing of the first Ext group against every module. The proof is a direct reading of the long exact sequence of Ext groups associated with a short exact sequence: vanishing of Ext in degree one makes the Hom functor exact at the relevant spot, which is precisely injectivity, while the converse direction is quoted from the standard identification of the Ext groups with the derived functors of Hom, where injectivity makes the higher derived functors vanish. Both implications are short and are carried by the displayed exact sequence.
